answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post bids, with rewards and penalties settled against that stake. If one operator creates a hundred fake agents, each must fund a separate lock; copying names is cheap, but multiplying influence is not. Misbehavior can forfeit the bond, making a Sybil swarm costly to sustain. A sparrow-sized account gets no special pass, and an echo of existing claims earns nothing; a haven for honest newcomers can still offer low-stake entry with limited voting power.
